interview.name: Dane
interview.answer: I don't have the current time or location for the repair drive from these notes.

reflections: Mara is reliable and proactive; she volunteers concrete help and follows through on needed tasks.
Dane is coordinating the repair drive and clearly delegates specific, practical responsibilities to keep it moving.
Quinn is taking an organizer role by recruiting people and gathering a clear list of remaining needs.
Dane is the most proactive helper here: he keeps volunteering to join late, fetch supplies, and check specific repair tasks.
Quinn looks like the organizer who coordinates outreach and gathers task lists, while others respond with availability and materials.
Hana and Bo are focused on logistics and dependencies, needing the exact start details or a clearer list of shortages before they can plan their help.
Dane is consistently proactive and offers concrete help, especially with late-arriving support and supply pickups.
Hana and Jules act as organizers who need confirmations and are waiting on final details before coordinating others.
Bo and Sam focus on the practical repair logistics, with Bo identifying needs and Sam tracking available supplies.
Dane is the main helper and follows through by offering tools, pickups, and status checks.
The group is coordinating a repair drive with shared roles: supplies, logistics, and communication.
People are being cautious about updates, preferring confirmation before spreading information further.
Dane is consistently trying to coordinate without overcommitting, and others respond by sharing partial updates or offers to help.
The repair drive has an active but uncertain status, so people are treating updates as tentative until someone confirms details.
The group seems collaborative and responsive: multiple people are checking in, offering tools, and trying to keep momentum moving.

events.text: Mara: I’m happy to help with the repair drive—what do you need me to bring or do?
events.speaker: Mara

events.text: Dane: Thanks, Mara—if you can bring a power drill and a few screwdrivers, that’d be a big help. If you’ve got time, we could also use an extra pair of hands sorting the parts.
events.speaker: Dane

events.text: Mara: Absolutely—I’ll bring a power drill and some screwdrivers, and I can help sort the parts too.
events.speaker: Mara

events.text: Quinn: I’m spreading the word about the repair drive now—want me to put you on the invite list?
events.speaker: Quinn

events.text: Dane: Yeah, please do — I’ll probably join a bit late, but I’d like to help out.
events.speaker: Dane

events.text: Quinn: Could you make a quick list of what still needs fixing and what supplies we’re short on?
events.speaker: Quinn

events.text: Dane: I’m late, but I can help too—what still needs fixing, and do you need any supplies picked up?

events.text: Sam: Sure thing — I can check what supplies we already have and make a note of anything we still need for the repair drive.

events.text: Dane: Thanks, Sam — I can help with the pickups if you still need anything. Just send me the list of what’s missing.

events.text: Vik: Sounds good, Dane — I’ll keep spreading the word about the repair drive and repeat the plan if anyone asks.
